directions.hookLine: Why did a carpenter abandon wood for plastic during an economic crisis?
directions.subheadline: LEGO embraced new technology to survive the depression.
directions.shortSummary: A carpenter's wooden toys fracture under economic pressure, forcing a shift to new materials. The shattered wood explodes into a modern plastic brick, proving LEGO's innovative survival.
directions.whyCompelling: It exposes a counterintuitive material pivot driven by historical necessity and technological curiosity.
directions.adAngle: Economic crisis forces a radical material evolution in toy making.
directions.visualEngine: A wooden toy car shatters and its splinters compress into a pristine plastic LEGO brick.

directions.hookLine: What happened when a global crisis killed a carpenter's livelihood?
directions.subheadline: The LEGO Group originated from desperate easy-to-sell wooden toys.
directions.shortSummary: A carpenter loses his trade to an economic crisis, forcing him to craft simple toys. Heavy ladders and tools melt down into small wooden cars, launching the LEGO brand.
directions.whyCompelling: It turns historical financial survival into a tangible, relatable transformation of raw materials.
directions.adAngle: A desperate career pivot creates a global toy legacy.
directions.visualEngine: Heavy wooden ladders and stepladders compress and shrink into a tiny 1932 wooden LEGO toy car.

directions.hookLine: How did a 1932 product line survive when everything else failed?
directions.subheadline: The first LEGO products laid the foundation for a global brand.
directions.shortSummary: A factory floor sits empty until the documented 1932 product line physically materializes. These initial wooden toys stack upward, building the foundation of the modern LEGO brand.
directions.whyCompelling: It visually anchors the massive modern brand to its humble, documented 1932 origins.
directions.adAngle: A documented 1932 product line literally builds the brand foundation.
directions.visualEngine: Empty space fills with assembling 1932 wooden toys that stack into a towering LEGO logo.

directions.hookLine: What hidden machinery saved a dying carpentry business?
directions.subheadline: LEGO used new processing methods to rationalize production.
directions.shortSummary: Old hand tools hide behind a curtain, replaced by the new machinery Ole Kirk Kristiansen adopted. The advanced gears and molds interlock, forming the precision of a LEGO brick.
directions.whyCompelling: It reveals the invisible industrial upgrade that enabled a carpenter to mass-produce toys.
directions.adAngle: Hidden production machinery drives the leap from craft to modern toy.
directions.visualEngine: Antique hand tools slide away as modern injection molds interlock to form a LEGO brick.

directions.hookLine: Why did a craftsman bet his future on an unfamiliar material?
directions.subheadline: LEGO's founder chased new materials to improve toy quality.
directions.shortSummary: A craftsman ignores traditional wood, reaching into a raw, unfamiliar block of plastic. The opaque material x-rays to reveal the internal structural precision of a modern LEGO brick.
directions.whyCompelling: It dramatizes the exact moment a founder's curiosity overcomes traditional manufacturing limits.
directions.adAngle: A founder's material curiosity unlocks a new standard of toy quality.
directions.visualEngine: A raw plastic block transitions via x-ray cutaway to expose the internal tubes of a LEGO brick.
